subject: Residency & networking stakeholder map — proposed next steps

Subject: Residency & networking stakeholder map — proposed next steps

Ashwin — thanks again for the time today. High-level recap and a proposed path forward so we’re aligned with StellarCare’s constraints and procurement timeline. Please correct anything I’ve misstated.

Summary of pain & drivers
- Regulatory/data residency: PHI must remain in US regions and we need evidence of audit log retention policy.
- Network isolation: preference for VPC peering (no public ingress), strict egress controls, and the ability to apply egress proxies; potential air-gap for specific workloads was raised as a long-term requirement.
- Procurement cadence: budget approval expected mid-September; procurement team wants a short SOW + an example PO.
- Risk tolerance: CISO (Dana) wants minimum external-facing surface and an ability to rotate keys via KMS/HSM.

What Redwood can commit to (first pass)
- Private/VPC hosting in US-only region with customer-managed peering and no public IPs on inference nodes.
- Audit logs (30/90 day retention options) and delivery via secure S3 bucket or push to your SIEM.
- Optional air-gapped on-prem bundle for regulated subsets (quote and deployment timeline required).
- Provide SOC2 Type II report and sample network diagram for procurement.

Open technical questions we need to resolve
1) Which specific CIDR blocks/environments will StellarCare provide for peering? Any transit gateway constraints?
2) Do you require egress block by default with allowlist for specific endpoints (e.g., monitoring, patching)?
3) For air-gap feasibility: which subsystems absolutely require zero external egress (model downloads, telemetry, metrics)?
4) KMS preference: AWS KMS vs. customer HSM — do you have a required vendor?

Proposed next steps
- Action A (this week): I’ll send our SOC2 and a high-level network diagram (attached).
- Action B (by Mon, 2026-08-31): StellarCare provides a short stakeholder map (CIDR, point-of-contact for network, and CISO concerns).
- Action C (w/in 2 weeks): Follow-up technical deep-dive (30–45 min) with your infra + our infra engineering.

Suggested meeting window for the deep-dive: Tue/Wed next week (09/01 or 09/02) — I'll let Ben coordinate calendar.

Attachments (sent inline): SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf (stub), stellarcare_network_diagram_v1.pdf (draft).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Raf — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifications and next items from our side:

Confirmations
- Residency: US-only is our hard requirement for now — production PHI must remain in US.
- Network: We will not allow public-facing IPs on inference nodes; peering is preferred.

Answers to open questions
1) CIDR: We'll provide two /16 ranges for testing and prod peering — infra will send exact blocks by COB Mon (08/31).
2) Egress: Default deny with allowlist is required. Monitoring endpoints (Datadog, internal patching) need exceptions — will provide hostnames.
3) Air-gap: For now, model weights can be staged via secure transfer for a subset of workloads; full air-gap (no egress) is a later phase but we need an architecture sketch during the deep-dive.
4) KMS: AWS KMS is preferred; HSM is optional but may be necessary for certain contracts.

Procurement note: looping in procurement and Dana (CISO) — Procurement requested a sample PO and your SOC2 (thank you for attaching). Dana — can you confirm whether StellarCare requires a vendor-supplied HSM for initial onboarding or if AWS KMS is okay?

Next steps from StellarCare
- Procurement will review attached PO template and revert with any redlines (procurement@stellarcare.health).
- Dana (CISO) will send a short list of minimum telemetry/telemetry-blocking requirements before the technical deep-dive.

I can join the engineering deep-dive next Tue 09/01 at 10:00 PT if that works — let me know and we’ll lock it.

Thanks,
Ashwin

Thanks all — quick technical clarifications from infra ops side so we can prep the deep-dive: 

- Egress allowlist: we can implement default deny and expose a managed egress proxy that only allows customer-approved FQDNs and IPs. We'll include an ops playbook for patching and package updates via a private mirror.
- Peering options: support both VPC peering and Transit Gateway. If you require shared services across accounts, Transit Gateway with route table segregation is recommended.
- KMS: Redwood supports AWS KMS and can integrate with customer CMKs in the same AWS org; for HSM-based flows we'll need an architecture call to scope connectivity and rotation.

I’ll prepare a short slide (2–3 pages) with: (a) proposed egress model, (b) sample peering diagram with route tables, (c) list of data-at-rest and data-in-transit controls. Rafael — I’ll attach that before the deep-dive. Ben — can you own scheduling once Ashwin confirms the 9/1 slot?
